extracted.intended_audience: freelance editors, editorial professionals, and clients seeking editorial services
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and descriptions of the range of editorial, publishing, writing, and related services offered by freelance editorial professionals, including examples of tasks, typical scope, and role expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing is, first and foremost, about taking an author’s words and turning them into a final product. It comprises a number of different types and is usually broken down into three specific types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General category framing; indicates editing covers developmental, line, and copyediting tasks and that editing is the process that transforms author drafts into a final product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Developmental editors (also called 'substantive,' 'structural,' or 'content' editors) deal with content, organization, and genre considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After reviewing a manuscript, they may provide an overall critique in a 'manuscript evaluation,' or an editorial letter outlining big-picture issues and offering suggestions for how to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Line editors work at the sentence or paragraph level of a manuscript, correcting errors but focusing mainly on improving the language and style of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line editing may be performed as a separate service, in conjunction with developmental editing after big-picture issues have been addressed, or in conjunction with copyediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyediting involves correcting spelling, grammar, usage, and punctuation, checking cross-references, and preparing the style sheets that guide consistency and accuracy across the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often considered the familiar, mechanical stage of editing focused on accuracy, consistency, and adherence to style conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading is among the last stages of getting a manuscript ready for publication; proofreaders check for typographical errors and formatting mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In traditional publishing, proofreading reviews a publisher’s 'proof'—comparing the latest stage of the project to the previous one to ensure all changes have been made correctly and that the document is ready to print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers create the text for everything composed of the written word: books, magazine articles, web content, blog posts, technical manuals, advertising and catalogue copy, speeches, dissertations, newsletter articles, annual reports, and much more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing is described as the foundation of all other editorial work; once text is written, the editorial process begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum developers work with educators and producers of educational materials to help organize materials and prepare them for use in the classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally, curriculum developers have training and experience in education at the relevant grade level and knowledge of applicable curriculum standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-for-Hire
rubrics_metrics.description: Work-for-hire writing is any writing contracted out to a writer by a client, who retains all rights to the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include articles, blog posts, web content, advertising copy, newsletters, and even full-length works; client retains rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ghostwriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ghostwriting is a particular kind of work-for-hire writing in which the writer writes on behalf of someone else using that person’s voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ghostwriters produce text that will be attributed to another person’s authorship—for example, autobiographies, memoirs, and other books—requiring the writer to capture the attributed author's voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading services encompass several forms of manuscript review performed by readers who provide feedback and insights about a work from the perspective of target readership or specific communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category includes beta reading, authenticity reading, and sensitivity reading, each with different focuses and expected reviewer backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Beta readers review manuscripts and offer authors feedback and insight, identifying errors, plot problems, inconsistencies, or unclear sections in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beta readers serve as a test audience representing the target readership and can help identify issues like overused tropes or missing elements; some beta readers may have particular expertise in the manuscript’s subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity readers review manuscripts looking for statements, portrayals, or perspectives that might misrepresent people from a given group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity reads are generally performed by members of the community referenced within the work to avoid misrepresentation of groups and the perpetuation of harmful stereotypes; may overlap with sensitivity reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity readers review manuscripts looking for statements, portrayals, or perspectives that might offend readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitivity reads are generally performed by members of communities other than the author’s own so they can provide helpful perspectives on language, characterization, and other aspects to help ensure material is acceptable to the broadest possible audience; may overlap with authenticity reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing services prepare text and materials for publication in print and/or digital formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This umbrella covers desktop and digital publishing, indexing, permissions management, research and fact-checking, and self-publishing assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desktop & Digital Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Desktop and digital publishers use desktop software or online platforms to prepare written material for publishing, creating publication-ready material by designing, laying out pages, formatting text, and incorporating illustrations or graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desktop publishers produce print material (books, brochures, flyers) and digital publishers produce material for electronic distribution (blogs, ebooks, enewsletters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexers create a book’s index—an alphabetical list of topics, names, places, and important terms used in the work that provides page numbers for where they can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing is usually done near the end of the project, when the final layout is ready and page numbers are unlikely to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissions editors verify the copyright status and ownership of works requiring permission to republish (written material or images whose copyright is held by someone other than the author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They either advise the author on how to obtain permissions or acquire the necessary permissions on the author’s behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Fact-Checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers and fact-checkers find information to support writing or verify information supplied by the writer or editor; fact-checkers review a manuscript and confirm the veracity of each statement claimed as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is deeper scrutiny than incidental fact-checking and is particularly important in journalism and historical writing—especially in fiction and narrative nonfiction, as opposed to scholarly writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-publishing Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial professionals can help authors navigate the self-publishing process by offering guidance on formatting, cover design, pricing, marketing, and other aspects of using major self-publishing platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support spans technical formatting through marketing strategy for independent publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting
rubrics_metrics.description: Consulting and coaching services help clients develop, refine, or complete works in progress and navigate publishing, printing, or production procedures and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The field is amorphous, covering inspiration and encouragement to practical advice and procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Coaches and consultants work with clients to develop, refine, or complete works in progress, offering inspiration, encouragement, and practical advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coaching is often done at the beginning of a project to get things off the ground or midway through a stuck project to get things going again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and Promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing and promotion specialists work with authors to publicize their work, developing marketing strategies and producing promotional materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services may include creating press releases, media kits, marketing collateral (print and electronic ads, postcards, bookmarks, swag), and helping authors develop their public platforms (websites, social media, blogs, podcasts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Project managers focus on projects already in the production workflow and work to push the project toward completion, supervising and coordinating the editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may hire copyeditors, proofreaders, indexers, and other professionals when necessary; in some fields this role is called 'managing editor' or 'production editor.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcriptionists listen to audio recordings (interviews, speeches, phone meetings, dictations) and convert them into long-form text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcriptionists are responsible for reviewing their written work for accuracy, spelling, and grammar; in specialized fields they might convert medical or legal records into written reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Translators recreate a work, published or unpublished, from one language into another, or review a translation for overall consistency or tone as well as accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may include full translation or revision for tone and consistency; accuracy and fidelity to original meaning are emphasized.
